title: LinkML extension libraries against the phase 0 model's bespoke pieces
question: Does linkml-map replace the change model's upcasters and name maps, does any extension library provide a schema diff or a correct expansion of inherits/include/minus, and does linkml-datalog fit beside the M19 rule language?
method: Throwaway environments on Python 3.14.10 with linkml-runtime 1.12.1 (linkml-map 0.5.4 and 0.6.0rc1 with pint 0.25.3; oaklib 0.7.4); a v1->v2 payload mapping with a rename, an enum rename, a nested class, absent and null fields and a polymorphic designates_type list; an inherits/include/minus expansion of a ClaimModality-like enum with in_subset properties; package metadata and import checks for the other libraries; a source and GitHub search for a schema diff.

agents.separation: read-only reviewer; scripts rerun by the coordinator into this folder

results.name: oak_expansion_correct_operators
results.note: inherits correct; include duplicated; minus ignored

conclusion: No LinkML extension library replaces a bespoke piece of the phase 0 model: linkml-map loses subclass fields and absent-vs-null and imports only with pint below 0.26; OAK's expander mishandles include and minus; no schema diff exists; linkml-datalog does not import on linkml-runtime 1.12.1. The plan keeps its own diff, upcasters, name maps and enum expansion, with linkml-map, schema-automator and oaklib as later options with triggers.
